items.title: Mount Everest
items.summary: Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth. Mount Everest is in the Himalayas, a tall mountain range in Asia.

items.title: Mount Kilimanjaro
items.summary: Kilimanjaro (or Kilimanjaro, which means "shining mountain" in Swahili), formerly Kaiser-Wilhelm-Spitze, is a mountain in northeastern Tanzania.

items.title: Alps
items.summary: The Alps (Italian: Alpi, French: Alpes, German: Alpen, Bavarian: Oipm, Romansh: Alps, Slovene: Alpe, Occitan: Aups, Alps) is the greatest mountain range of Europe. It reaches from Austria and Slovenia in the east; through Italy, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and Germany; to France in the west.

items.title: Andes
items.summary: The Andes are a mountain range along the western coast of South America.

items.title: Himalayas
items.summary: The Himalayas (from Sanskrit हिमालय) are a mountain range located north of the Indian subcontinent.

items.title: Rocky Mountains
items.summary: The Rocky Mountains, often called The Rockies, are a range of mountains in the western United States and Canada. They stretch from the northernmost part of British Columbia, in Western Canada, to New Mexico, in the Southwestern United States.

items.title: Volcano
items.summary: A volcano is a mountain that has lava (hot, liquid rock) coming out from a magma chamber under the ground, or did have in the past. Volcanoes are formed by the movement of tectonic plates.

items.title: Mount Fuji
items.summary: Mount Fuji (富士山, Fuji-san) is the tallest mountain in Japan, at

items.title: Krakatoa
items.summary: Krakatoa (Indonesian name: Krakatau) is an active volcano in the Sunda Strait, Indonesia. There are many different ways the name has been spelled.

items.title: Mount Vesuvius
items.summary: Mount Vesuvius (Italian: Monte Vesuvio, Latin: Mons Vesuvius) is a stratovolcano on the Gulf of Naples, Italy. It is about 8 kilometres (5 mi) east of Naples.

items.title: Mount St. Helens
items.summary: Mount St. Helens is a volcano in the U.S. state of Washington. It is 96 miles (154 km) south of Seattle and 53 miles (85 km) northeast of Portland, Oregon.

items.title: Popocatépetl
items.summary: Popocatépetl (also called El popo or Don Goyo) is an active volcano. The volcano is the second highest mountain in Mexico after Pico de Orizaba (5,610m).

items.title: Mount Etna
items.summary: Mount Etna is a volcano on the east coast of Sicily, part of southern Italy. It is the largest active volcano in Europe.

items.title: Mount Rainier
items.summary: Mount Rainier (), known to Native Americans in the region as Tahoma, Tacoma, Tacobet, or təqʷubəʔ, is a large volcano in the Cascade Range of the Pacific Northwest located in Mount Rainier National Park about 59 miles (95 km) south of Seattle.

items.title: Mount Merapi
items.summary: Mount Merapi (Gunung Merapi in Indonesian) is a volcano in Indonesia. It is on the island of Java.

items.title: Mount Tambora
items.summary: Mount Tambora (8°14’41”S, 117°59’35”E) is an active volcano in Indonesia. It is on top of a subduction zone.

items.title: Mount Aso
items.summary: Mount Aso (阿蘇山, Aso-san) or Aso Volcano is the largest active volcano in Japan and among the largest in the world.

items.title: Plate tectonics
items.summary: Plate tectonics is a theory of geology. It explains movement of the Earth's lithosphere.

items.title: Pacific Ring of Fire
items.summary: The Pacific Ring of Fire is an arc around the Pacific Ocean where many volcanoes and earthquakes are formed. The area is also called the Pacific Rim, a term which refers to the coastal areas of the countries round the Pacific.

items.title: Nile
items.summary: The Nile (النيل an-nīl) is a river in Africa. It is the longest river on Earth (estimated as 6,682 km or 4,152 miles), though other rivers carry more water.

items.title: Amazon River
items.summary: The Amazon River (also called Rio Amazonas in Portuguese and Spanish) is the largest river in the world by the amount or volume of water it carries. It flows through the tropical forests of South America, mainly in Brazil.

items.title: Yangtze River
items.summary: The Yangtze River, or Yangzi (Simple Chinese: 扬子江 / Traditional Chinese: 揚子江), or Chang Jiang (Simple Chinese: 长江 / Traditional Chinese: 長江), is the longest River in China and Asia, as well as the world's fourth longest river (after the Amazon, the Nile and the Mississippi-Missouri-Jefferson river…

items.title: Mississippi River
items.summary: The Mississippi River is a river in the United States. It is the 11th longest river in the world.

items.title: Danube
items.summary: The Danube (Latin name Hister) is the second-longest river in Europe (the Volga is the longest). It is the longest river of the European Union.

items.title: Congo River
items.summary: The Congo River (also known as Zaire River) is the largest river in Africa. Its overall length of 4,700 km (2,922 miles) makes it the second longest in Africa (after the Nile).

items.title: Ganges
items.summary: The Ganges (English pronunciation: /ˈɡændʒiːz/ GAN-jeez), also called the Ganga (Sanskrit: गङ्गा, Hindi: गंगा, ; Ganga IPA: [ˈɡəŋɡaː]; Bengali: গঙ্গা Gonga), is the third largest river on the Indian subcontinent by discharge. The Ganges river is named after a Hindu goddess called Ganga.

items.title: Murray River
items.summary: The Murray River is the longest river in Australia, about 2,508 km (1,558 mi). It starts high in the Snowy Mountains and flows mainly west.

items.title: Niger River
items.summary: The Niger River is the main river of western Africa. It is over 4180 km (2500 miles) long.

items.title: Rhine River
items.summary: The Rhine River (German: Rhein, French: Rhin, Dutch: Rijn) is 1,230 kilometres (760 mi) long. Its name comes from the Celtic word "renos", which means 'raging flow'.

items.title: Mekong River
items.summary: The Mekong River is a river in southeast Asia. It flows through many countries: China, Burma, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, and finally Vietnam.

items.title: Atlantic Ocean
items.summary: The Atlantic Ocean is the world's second largest ocean. It covers a total area of about 106,400,000 square kilometres (41,100,000 square miles), about 20 percent of the Earth's surface.

items.title: Arctic Ocean
items.summary: The Arctic Ocean is the ocean around the North Pole. The most northern parts of Eurasia and North America are around the Arctic Ocean.

items.title: Great Barrier Reef
items.summary: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef stretching over 1,400 miles. It is near the coast of Queensland, Australia.

items.title: Sahara
items.summary: The Sahara, in North Africa, is the largest desert in the world except for Antarctica. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.
